key_insight: Increasing the detonation-spray barrel filling ratio from 43% to 53% produced denser Cr3C2–NiCr coatings with better wear resistance, even though friction increased.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing spray barrel filling ratio is a practical way to improve carbide coating integrity and durability for high-wear industrial components.
method: Detonation-sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr coatings at 43% and 53% barrel filling ratios
Compared microstructure and phase composition using microscopy and X-ray diffraction
Evaluated dry sliding wear with ball-on-disc tests at 10 and 15 N and 5 and 10 cm/s
evidence_signal: The 53% coating showed lower porosity, retained Cr3C2/NiCr as dominant phases with minor Cr7C3 formation, and reached a minimum wear rate of 1.23 × 10^-4 mm3/(m·N).
watch_item: The improved wear resistance at 53% came with a higher coefficient of friction, so the optimal setting may depend on whether low friction or maximum wear life is the priority.
paper_title: Effect of Barrel Filling Ratio on the Microstructure, Phase Composition and Tribological Performance of Detonation-Sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr Coatings
